narrative_synthesis: The meta today is rent anxiety plus a house-hacking pile-on. Drafts: (1) a calm 'yes, house hacking is being a landlord, that's the point' take, (2) a 'where the rent actually goes' breakdown without made-up numbers, (3) a one-line 'first number you check' reply magnet.

drafts.draft_en:
"House hacking is just being a landlord."

Yes. That's the point.

Buy a Philly duplex, live in one side, rent the other. The tenant helps pay the note while you learn the business with one unit.

Call it whatever you want. It's how a lot of us start building legacy.
drafts.pattern: reply-to-the-meta on the house-hacking pile-on (nissyiam 2.5k) + Philly local angle + legacy theme
drafts.video_tip: Stand in front of a duplex or rowhome pair, 20-30s. Read the quote off your phone in the first 2 seconds, then say 'Yes. That's the point.' No numbers or return promises.

drafts.draft_en:
Renters think the landlord keeps the whole rent check.

Here's where it actually goes:

1/ The mortgage
2/ Taxes and insurance
3/ Repairs and maintenance
4/ Reserves for vacancies
5/ Whatever's left

That last line is smaller than people think. Underwrite all five before you buy.
drafts.pattern: rent-transparency breakdown (theficouple 3.3k) aimed at today's rent-anxiety star, numbered list, no invented figures
drafts.video_tip: Hold up five sticky notes or fingers, 25-35s. If you add numbers, use a real deal of yours or label them as example numbers on screen.

drafts.draft_en: Before you buy your first Philly rental, what's the one number you check first?
